clips.title: The Definition of Ready - Agile Software Development
clips.why: Teams already have a name for a ticket that is clear enough to start: the Definition of Ready. Our readiness check is a definition of ready that a model applies in seconds.
look: What "ready to work on" means: the team can start without coming back with questions. That is our ready verdict.
The INVEST letters. Listen for Small and Testable: they are our size and how_to_check fields.
A ticket that fails these tests is not thrown away; it goes back to be made ready. That is the difference between ask and hand back.
clips.after: Our check writes the same judgement as JSON, before any machine starts, so the workflow can act on it without a meeting.

clips.title: Machine Learning Fundamentals: The Confusion Matrix
clips.why: The clearest short explanation of the table you build in the lab, including a three-by-three version like ours with ready, ask and hand back.
look: Which side of the table he uses for the truth and which for the prediction. The lab puts the person's label in the rows; the diagonal means agreement either way.
Comparing two matrices: the same total can hide very different mistakes.
The three-by-three matrix: every cell off the diagonal is one specific confusion between two answers.
clips.after: In our matrix the cell that matters most is the person's hand back against the model's ready, a false ready, and one of those is enough to keep the check switched off.

clips.title: 3. Tutorial: How to create an LLM judge and align with human labels
clips.why: The same order of work we follow before switching the readiness check on: label examples yourself, write the judge, compare it with your labels, and only then use it.
look: "Be the judge": she labels the dataset by hand before any model sees it, like our 30 past tickets.
The judge is prompt work for a classifier: a fixed set of labels, not free text.
Evaluating the judge against the human labels comes before using it, never after.
clips.after: Our readiness check is that kind of classifier with three labels, and the comparison with hand labels is a step in the plan, not an extra.

practice.q: Which parts of RH-1234 does the readiness check read?

options.text: The summary, the description, the comments and the titles of linked tickets
options.why: Text only. That is enough to judge whether the ticket is clear, and it keeps attachments out of the prompt.

options.text: Everything, including attachments and screenshots, so nothing is missed
options.why: Attachments are where real customer and patient data hides. The check never reads them.

options.text: The ticket and the code it is about, so it can judge the size
options.why: The check runs before any machine, with no repo. Reading code is the planner's job.

practice.q: RH-1301 says only: "Make the projects page better." Which verdict fits?

options.why: Fuzzy is the size, but nobody can say how to check "better", so it is not ready.

options.text: ask, with questions such as "What is wrong with the page today?"
options.why: The ticket can become a job once the requester says what better means. One answer away is ask, not hand back.
Hand back is for tickets that cannot be done as written, such as real data or an area outside the pilot. This one needs a sentence, not a new ticket.

practice.q: Finish the rule: an ask, or a ready ticket that is bigger than small, goes to the requester first.
practice.hint: The smallest of the three sizes.
practice.why: Only a small, ready ticket goes straight to planning. Bigger and fuzzy tickets get their questions first, because an answer is cheaper than a plan built on a guess.

practice.q: The Agent SDK validates structured output with JSON Schema draft-07. Finish the conversion so the SDK accepts the schema.
practice.hint: Look at the last line of the schema in the Understand step.
practice.why: Without the target, zod writes draft 2020-12, which the SDK refuses.

practice.q: In the comparison with hand labels, which disagreement costs the most?

options.why: The requester answers one extra question. Cheap.
The ticket goes back when one question would have done. Annoying, but no machine runs.
Real work starts on a ticket that should never have started: a machine, a plan, maybe an area outside the pilot.

practice.q: Put the start of RH-1234's run in order.
items: You assign RH-1234 to Nova in Jira
Within a minute the Jira poll finds it and reads the changelog: you are the requester
The poll starts the run nova:RH-1234
The readiness check reads the ticket text and answers ready, size small
Only now does the run claim a lite VM to write the plan
practice.why: Everything before the last step runs without a machine. The VM is the first expensive thing, so it comes after the verdict.
